question: Can one exposure to advanced coding or computer-use actions make our model permanently capable in arbitrary new environments, the most advanced agent, or sentient?
verdict: The universal conclusion is not supported. A narrow result is real: one externally stored, verified operator rule transferred to different code in the same bug family. The full repair harness still solved 0/2 cases without that stored rule. Durable external memory is not the same as permanent, general model learning.

one_stored_rule_transfer.demonstration: total = amount * rate // 1000 -> total = amount * rate / 1000
one_stored_rule_transfer.scope: The rule was derived and stored outside the repair loop. This shows retrieval/generalization of one verified rule within its bug family; it does not show automatic crystallization from one attempt, a weight update, or arbitrary-task transfer.

cross_episode_memory.interpretation: The tested memory was addressed by a changing task sentence; it did not recall across those episodes.

change.interpretation: The aggregate rate movement is within the prior +/-2.7 percentage-point noise band; do not call it a clear aggregate improvement. Form-sequence rose from 0/5 to 5/5 and form-sequence-2 from 0/5 to 4/5, while other task results moved both up and down.

what_one_demo_can_and_cannot_mean.can: Save a successful, tested rule or trajectory in durable external memory and retrieve it later when the same relevant conditions hold. Similar demonstrations can also help inside a model's current prompt.
what_one_demo_can_and_cannot_mean.cannot_be_inferred: One exposure does not establish that the model has extracted the right rule, that it will retrieve it, that it applies in a different task family or software environment, that it will compose it with other skills, or that model weights changed.
what_one_demo_can_and_cannot_mean.persistence: A database entry can remain on disk. Its existence is persistent storage; it is not proof of permanent general capability.

first_principles_and_noise.current_measurement_rule: One repair is about +0.77 percentage points on this 130-task score; the single-run noise band is about +/-2.7 points. A one-task change is not evidence of a robust capability change. Compare the same per-task outcomes, use repeated runs, and test held-out cases.
first_principles_and_noise.consequence: A successful action is not a learned procedure until its preconditions, procedure, and verified outcome are stored and later recalled. An action is not a repair until the candidate is applied and the null/broken policy fails while the repaired policy passes.

external_research.finding: A similar demonstration can help on a scoped benchmark.
external_research.result: The AppWorld study reports that one similar task trajectory raised a zero-shot agent's task completion by 29 points on that benchmark. This is in-context use of a supplied demonstration, not proof of permanent weight learning or transfer to arbitrary environments.

external_research.finding: Memory is not a solved universal mechanism.
external_research.result: EvoMemBench (2026) evaluates memory within and across episodes and reports that current memory methods are not a general solution; which memory helps depends on task and context.

external_research.finding: Training weights can forget earlier tasks.
external_research.result: One 2026 sequential fine-tuning study reports Llama 4 Maverick's first-task score falling from 89.3% to 67.2% after three later tasks. This is a study result, not a measurement of our model.

external_research.finding: Long computer workflows are not solved by high short-task scores.
external_research.result: OSWorld 2.0 reports 108 long workflows; the best tested setup in that paper completed 20.6% under its strict 500-step measure. This is evidence about that benchmark and run, not a universal ceiling.

external_research.finding: Coding leaderboard numbers depend on the tested system and harness.
external_research.result: SWE-bench Verified documents separate full-agent results from its same-harness mini-SWE-agent comparison and warns that harness versions matter. Our 2-case benchmark cannot establish a world ranking.

sentience: No. These measurements show code execution, rule storage, and retrieval. They provide no evidence of subjective experience or sentience.
smartest_next_steps: Use the live-page evidence, not task source or hidden answer variables, to fix the shared angle-task failure: right-angle and bisect-angle both route to a generic click that presses Submit (sole-done, 0/5 each). Build the point from visible SVG geometry, read the point back, then submit.

Treat the login/booking and geometry/tab batches as tuning samples; do not report them as held-out transfer. After the angle fix, rerun the two tasks at 5 reps and also run regression checks before making any claim.
Then investigate the separate click-shape, click-tab, and count-sides misses from their rendered page state; one task-family fix must not be described as universal computer use.

For any proposed learning change, compare the unchanged/null policy and repaired policy on the same tasks with repeated runs and per-task diffs. Keep external memory as verified procedures with explicit preconditions and read-back.
Do not claim permanent universal computer use, sentience, or world leadership from one successful case or a 0/2 coding benchmark.

follow_up_batches.evidence_classification: These tasks were already part of the r180/r181 130-task measurement. The R182 reruns are diagnostic/tuning data, not an independent held-out validation set.
